title: Customer-tailored prefetch & batch ops safety harness
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Deliver an automated, auditable pipeline that recommends and safely applies per-customer and per-route batching + KV-prefetch configurations driven by segmentation (customer tiers, route profiles). The system must produce conservative suggestions, run deterministic dry-runs against recent traffic traces, and support staged canary apply with automated rollback on SLO/quality regressions.

Scope:
- Recommendation engine that suggests: batching window, max_batch_size, preferred cache prefetch length, and whether to use route-specific allowlists/denylists.
- Policy layer to map customers into tiers (free/prod/enterprise) and apply minimum safety constraints per tier.
- Dry-run simulator that replays traffic for the last 72h to estimate cost delta, latency change, and model quality regressions using saved prompt testsets.
- Safe apply orchestration: canary rollout (config percentages), telemetry guardrails (latency P99, error rate, quality delta), automated rollback and notification playbook.
- Audit trail and CLI/API to force-apply, abort, or schedule rollbacks.

Non-goals: full model quantization tooling, UI polish for Console dashboards (follow-up PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation engine outputs suggestions with estimated cost delta and confidence score for 95% of customer-route combos in test bucket.
Dry-run simulation provides time-series of token-level cost, P50/P95 latency, and quality regression score for suggested config.
Canary apply mechanism supports staged rollout (0.5%, 2%, 10%, 50%) with automated evaluation windows and abort/rollback triggers.
Safety guards enforce tier-level minimums (e.g., enterprise routes cannot drop below X latency SLO) and respect explicit allowlists/denylists.
All config changes are recorded in the platform audit log with author, diff, and roll-forward/back metadata.
Runbook for manual intervention and incident paging tested in staging with simulated failure modes.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: dry-run on sandbox using last-7-day traffic replay (team validation)
Stage 1: canary 0.5% customers for 4h with automated metric checks
Stage 2: expand to 2% for 8h, run deeper quality checks (prompt-set evals)
Stage 3: 10% for 24h, decision gate for 50%/global based on metrics and stakeholder sign-off
Emergency: immediate global rollback if P99 latency increases > 30% or error rate > 1% absolute
implementation_notes: We will reuse the policy engine's rule DSL; add two new predicates: customer_tier() and route_profile().
Dry-run uses request-level replay with stochastic sampling to bound compute. Store simulated KV hits/misses to estimate cost impact.
Prefetch decisions will default to conservative lengths for Free/Tier1, aggressive for Enterprise with opt-in allowlist.
All applies go through the orchestrator which creates a transaction-like config bundle with canary segments and telemetry hooks.
Rollback is implemented as versioned config revert with a time-window hold to prevent flapping; emergency abort bypasses hold.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive recommendations causing regressions in output quality. Mitigation: quality_regression_score threshold + prompt-set eval before any >2% rollout.
Risk: Incomplete segmentation misclassifies high-traffic tenant. Mitigation: default conservative caps, require explicit enterprise opt-in for aggressive policies.
Risk: Telemetry gaps during canary causing false positives. Mitigation: preflight instrumentation check and synthetic traffic probes in each canary window.
Risk: Rollback flapping due to noisy signals. Mitigation: require sustained breach for two consecutive evaluation windows before global rollback.
